items.heading: ### Placing a feature into a relation table
items.text: Known issue: a DataField, DataColumn or RelationColumn that `fill` or `update <table> --add feature` creates gets an explicit `label` at creation. The label is the member name with only its first letter capitalized (for example `TotalLabel`, not `Total Label`), and the generated table shows that value as the column header. The generator splits words only when `label` is unset, so the raw member name reaches the UI. Workaround: set a readable header on every such column with `update <column-fqn> --set label=<Header text>` (for example `<TO>::<TO>_Table::<member>`), including columns added after `fill`, and check it with `query esm DataColumn --select label`.

items.heading: Model shape
items.text: Generated UI pages follow from the entity and its access. Keep the View and Update pages for administrators. The entity-level createable and deleteable flags are not read by the generator. The Create and Delete actions come from the flags on the administrator's access to Configuration: keep createable and deleteable false on that access, so the generated UI shows no Create or Delete action. The update form should be pre-filled with current values; see [frontend.md](frontend.md).

items.heading: Practice > Practice notes: pick a customization level per actor
items.text: - Two actors are the tested shape. A third actor breaks the generated admin frontend build (known issue): `./judo.sh build` stops at `pnpm run format` (biome) with `Declarations inside of a import declaration may not have duplicates`, for example `import type { CsvFile, CsvFile, CsvFileStored, CsvFileStored }`, when an operation has an input and an output of the same type. The template emits one import per entry of `getApiImportsForPage`, and that list is built from a `HashSet<ClassType>` that deduplicates by object identity, so two ClassType objects for one class produce duplicate lines. Present with any third actor (human or system, anonymous or not, with or without an access) and gone when the third actor is removed. Workaround: keep the frontend to two actors and route the extra operation through an existing actor (for example a technical admin call); do not add a third actor to a module that has such operations.
items.replaces: - The pattern extends to three or more actors; some can be dashboard-only placeholders. Actors can differ in authentication (for example an anonymous public actor next to authenticated staff actors).

items.heading: Platform base
items.text: - A `Placeholder` element of the UI model can also be marked as a custom implementation. The generator turns it into a spacer that keeps its grid position and copies the flag, so the scaffold `register<Interface>CustomImplementation` is generated for it and the page renders the component in a `ComponentProxy` at that position, with the generated empty spacer as fallback. Use it for one region of a page. A placeholder cannot replace a whole view; for that, mark a container (see the custom view notes in the model blueprints).

items.heading: When No Manual Step Is Needed
items.text: It is a startup log, not a build failure: run the schema upgrade for that database (see the migration rules below). If the check itself cannot run, the log shows the same error with a `NoClassDefFoundError` for `hu.blackbelt.epsilon.runtime.execution.contexts.EolExecutionContext`, and a schema upgrade does not help. Known issue: the RDBMS model bundle imports the Epsilon runtime packages as optional, and the `judo-meta-rdbms` feature does not install the `epsilon-runtime` feature, so the compatibility check fails when the database already holds a model version. Workaround: add the `epsilon-runtime` feature to the application's Karaf boot features, restart, and check that the `Could not find compatible schema model` line is gone. An empty database does not reach this check: the prehook creates the model store and the schema on start.

items.heading: ## Frontend Build Recovery
items.text: **Known issue: UI validation errors print as `{}: {}`.** The UI validation step logs through `StringBuilderLogger`, which formats messages with `String.format`. Slf4j-style `{}` placeholders are not replaced, so each failing UI constraint is logged as the bare line `{}: {}` with no constraint name or message. The Java validator path (`UiJavaValidator`) logs this way; the build reaches it when the Epsilon UI executor cannot be loaded, and then logs `Validator class ... not found. Using fallback.` Workaround: run `judo-cli -m <model-path> validate`, which prints each UI finding as `error ui <constraint> <element>: <message>`, and fix the reported constraints. Platform fix: format the placeholders in `StringBuilderLogger` the way slf4j does.
